commissionerKeeperNote: Keepers shouldn't be a fight — the system rewards good drafting and smart in-season moves. Raising keeper cost by a round each year makes you weigh a player's real value and frees up players who used to be locked away. Suggestions welcome.

rows.rule: Each team may keep two players.
A keeper costs the round he was drafted in the prior year — unless he has been kept multiple years.
Each additional year you keep a player, his keeper cost moves up one round.
Draft order follows final regular season standings for teams that miss the playoffs.

rows.example: Example: Both eliminated in the quarterfinal — Team 1 (9-5) gets pick 6, Team 2 (7-7) gets pick 5.
rows.rule: As teams are eliminated in the playoffs, the team with the better record picks later.
If records are tied, the team with more regular season points picks later.

rows.example: Exception: if you originally drafted him, he keeps his original draft spot — waiver rules do not apply.
rows.rule: A keeper claimed off waivers last season costs an 8th round pick.

rows.example: Example: Two 3rd rounders — the better player costs a 2nd, the other a 3rd.
rows.rule: Keeping two players from the same round: the higher-ranked player (Yahoo rankings) costs one round earlier; the other keeps that round.
Keeping two 1st rounders: the higher-ranked player (Yahoo) costs a 1st, the other a 2nd.

rows.example: Exception: if he was claimed off waivers before the trade, he costs an 8th round pick.
rows.rule: A keeper acquired by trade costs the round he was drafted in the prior year.
Roster players and draft picks may be traded before the draft.
Pick limits: 16 picks max (one per draft selection), and 14 minimum if you keep two players.
Offseason trading closes one week before keeper selections are due.
Waiver-claimed players may be traded at 8th round keeper value.
